answer: In an agent marketplace, each voting identity must lock a fixed bond before joining a decision. An attacker seeking a majority cannot turn one deposit into many votes: every fake identity needs its own bond, tying up capital for the voting period. If a signed vote is provably duplicated, the bond is forfeited. A legitimate agent selling nectar faces the same rule, but a sybil campaign at the market's nadir must fund a much larger ripple of identities.
